title_en: Liu Yukun v. Zheng Xianqiu — divorce and property division dispute
keywords_en: civil; divorce dispute; property division; second instance; High People's Court; Heilongjiang Province; natural person; Marriage Law; Law on the Protection of Rights and Interests of Women; Civil Procedure Law; whether medals constitute community property (of husband and wife); whether bonuses should be divided; affirm the original judgment; divorce; disabled athlete; medals; bonuses; protect the rights and interests of the wife and children; marriage
full_text_en:
Liu Yukun v. Zheng Xianqiu — divorce and property division dispute

Plaintiff: Liu Yukun, female, born on December 28, 1958, typist at the Metal Structure Branch of the First Heavy Machinery Plant, Fularji District, Qiqihar City, Heilongjiang Province. Address: No. 1-6, 26-10 Tiexi, Fularji District, Qiqihar City.

Defendant: Zheng Xianqiu, male, born on October 20, 1957, worker at the same factory as the plaintiff. Address same as above.

Plaintiff Liu Yukun filed a lawsuit with the Qiqihar Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province regarding divorce and property division with the defendant Zheng Xianqiu.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff and the defendant Zheng Xianqiu were incompatible in personality after marriage, and they had different ideals, careers, and interests. Over 13 years of marriage, they had never cultivated and established true marital affection. The defendant interfered unreasonably with the plaintiff's participation in necessary social activities and treatment for her physical disability. After 1984, the plaintiff overcame difficulties unimaginable to ordinary people and won three gold medals at the first National Disabled Persons' Games. These achievements increased the psychological gap between them, and the defendant subsequently violently interfered with the plaintiff's participation in competitions, injuring her and causing her to be hospitalized. The plaintiff and the defendant have been living separately since May 1992, and their marital affection has indeed broken down. The plaintiff requests the court to grant a divorce and to divide the property according to law.

Defendant's Defense: The defendant and the plaintiff had a good marital foundation. When the plaintiff lost her legs, it was the defendant who voluntarily married her. After marriage, the defendant undertook all household chores, childcare, and the plaintiff's daily care. The plaintiff's multiple medal wins at international and domestic disabled persons' games were inseparable from the defendant's support and care. If the plaintiff insists on divorce, the child should be raised by the defendant, and the plaintiff must pay a monthly support of RMB 150. The house should be occupied by the defendant. Of the 17 medals, the defendant should receive half. Of the RMB 290,000 in prize money, the defendant claims RMB 190,000. The marital property acquired after marriage should be divided according to law.

Facts Found by the Court: The plaintiff Liu Yukun and the defendant Zheng Xianqiu worked at the same unit. They fell in love freely in early 1979, registered their marriage on June 10 of the same year, and gave birth to a son, Zheng Yang, the following year. Due to differences in personality and interests, they failed to consult each other on family matters and often quarreled over trivial issues, causing their marital affection to gradually break down. The parties began living separately in May 1992. On January 29, 1993, a quarrel broke out between them, and during the physical altercation, Zheng Xianqiu struck Liu Yukun's left eye, causing her to be hospitalized for treatment, further deteriorating their relationship. On February 16, 1993, Liu Yukun filed a divorce lawsuit with this court based on a breakdown of marital affection. After multiple mediation attempts were unsuccessful, Liu Yukun insisted on divorce, while Zheng Xianqiu disagreed. Their minor son, Zheng Yang, now 14 years old, expressed his wish to live with his mother, Liu Yukun. The current residence, a two-bedroom-and-kitchen apartment, is owned by the Heavy Machinery Plant. The family's jointly owned property includes: 1 gold ring, 1 gold necklace, 3 various wheelchairs (carts), 1 bicycle, 1 washing machine, 1 refrigerator, 1 color TV, 1 game console, 1 tape recorder, 1 VCR, 1 set of combination furniture, 1 set of corner sofa, 1 set of three-seat sofa, 1 single bed, 1 double bed, 1 desk, 2 carpets, etc. Liu Yukun won 17 medals (including 16 gold medals and 1 bronze medal) and prize money of RMB 59,012 from her participation in various international and domestic disabled persons' games. The prize money was used for: a pair of artificial limbs from Tianjin Changting Prosthetics Company costing RMB 22,000; and medical treatment, travel, and other expenses totaling RMB 38,612.83.

The above facts are confirmed by materials and receipts provided by the China Disabled Persons' Federation, the State Sports Commission, the Heilongjiang Provincial Sports Commission, the Heilongjiang Provincial Disabled Persons' Federation, the Qiqihar City Sports Commission, the Qiqihar City Disabled Persons' Federation, the Guangzhou City Sports Commission, and Tianjin Changting Prosthetics Company.

Opinion of the Court: Although the plaintiff Liu Yukun and the defendant Zheng Xianqiu have been married for many years and have a son, they have failed to be mutually understanding and accommodating in their shared life. Having lived separately for one year, their marital affection has indeed broken down, and there is no possibility of reconciliation. Pursuant to Article 25 of the Marriage Law of the PRC, where the marital affection of both parties has indeed broken down and mediation is ineffective, divorce shall be granted. Since their minor son Zheng Yang expressed his wish to live with his mother Liu Yukun, the child's wishes should be respected. The leased apartment is a self-managed property of the Heavy Machinery Plant and should be adjusted by the property rights unit in accordance with Article 44, Paragraph 3 of the Law of the PRC on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests, following the principle of "giving consideration to the rights and interests of women and children." The medals are symbols of honor personally obtained by Liu Yukun and should not be divided as jointly owned marital property. The verified prize money of RMB 59,012 has already been used by Liu Yukun for artificial limbs, medical treatment, travel, etc., and there is no remaining deposit. Zheng Xianqiu's claim that Liu Yukun has prize money of RMB 290,000 lacks evidence and is not recognized. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 31 of the Marriage Law of the PRC, which provides that "upon divorce, the jointly owned property of the husband and wife shall be disposed of by agreement between the parties; if an agreement cannot be reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment based on the specific circumstances of the property and the principle of giving consideration to the rights and interests of women and children," this court renders the following judgment on May 6, 1994:

1. Divorce is granted to the plaintiff Liu Yukun and the defendant Zheng Xianqiu.
2. Their minor son Zheng Yang (14 years old) shall be raised by Liu Yukun. Zheng Xianqiu shall pay monthly child support of RMB 60 until Zheng Yang becomes financially independent.
3. Jointly owned property: The gold ring, gold necklace, wheelchairs, washing machine, vacuum cleaner, and other items shall belong to Liu Yukun; the bicycle, combination furniture, refrigerator, color TV, tape recorder, and other items shall belong to Zheng Xianqiu. The personal clothing of each party shall belong to that party.
4. The 17 medals shall belong to Liu Yukun.

Court costs of RMB 50 shall be borne equally by Liu Yukun and Zheng Xianqiu, each paying RMB 25.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the defendant Zheng Xianqiu appealed to the Heilongjiang High People's Court, arguing that the medals and prize money obtained by the plaintiff Liu Yukun during the marriage should be divided equally.

Judgment of the Heilongjiang High People's Court: The court finds that the marital affection between the appellant Zheng Xianqiu and the appellee Liu Yukun has indeed broken down. After multiple unsuccessful mediation attempts by the original court, the judgment granting divorce to Liu Yukun and Zheng Xianqiu, awarding custody of their minor son Zheng Yang to Liu Yukun, and dividing the jointly owned property was correct and reasonable. As to the issue of the medals and prize money won by Liu Yukun in international and domestic disabled persons' sports competitions, investigations by the State Sports Commission and the China Disabled Persons' Federation confirmed that from the first National Disabled Persons' Games in 1984 to the 1992 Paralympic Games, Liu Yukun won a total of 17 medals and prize money of RMB 59,012. Although the above medals and prize money were obtained during the marriage, the medals are symbols of honor personal to Liu Yukun as a disabled athlete and have a specific personal nature; they should not be divided as jointly owned marital property. The prize money received has already been used for Liu Yukun's artificial limbs, medical treatment, and other expenses, constituting a joint family expenditure, and there is no remaining property to divide. Zheng Xianqiu's request for an equal division has no legal basis. In summary, the judgment of the first instance court has clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law. The appellant Zheng Xianqiu's grounds of appeal are insufficient and are not supported by this court. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court, on December 1, 1994, renders the following judgment: The appeal of appellant Zheng Xianqiu is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
